title: Two-page passback: Velma Hart (contrasting signals)
summary: Rapid passback after loop with Velma Hart — interesting mix of deep systems intuition and surface-level unfamiliarity with our operational patterns. Strong candidate-level signals on debugging and performance, weaker on rollout tradeoffs and service-level product thinking.
scorecard:
Overall: 6/10
Technical (system design): 7/10 - solid mental model for caching, KV retention, and memory-bound inference.
Code pairing: 6/10 - readable, pragmatic but left out some edgecases in concurrency.
Production judgment: 5/10 - conservative but fuzzy on rollout/rollback playbooks.
Collaboration/communication: 6/10 - clear, asks questions but tends to anchor on own mental models.
Culture fit: 6/10 - pragmatic, curious, but not clearly excited by product-level tradeoffs we prioritize.
recommendation: Consider for IC4/IC5 runtime engineer (backend-heavy role) with a clear onboarding plan to ramp product/rollout fluency. Stronger fit if paired with senior platform PM/Eng manager who can mentor on SLAs and customer-facing tradeoffs. Not immediately recommend for senior on-call owner without follow-up training.
raw_notes:
Start-time: 10:40am. Pairing task: implement small LRU-backed KV cache shim and reason about eviction under bursty tails.
- Approach: designed a two-tier cache (in-memory LRU + small persistent prefix cache). Focused on simple invariants and measurable metrics (hit rate, eviction rate).
- Wins: called out the hot-key problem and suggested hedging TTLs by request-side backoff. Also sketched a cheap probabilistic admission filter to avoid cache pollution.
- Misses: did not explicitly account for multi-tenant fairness or per-tenant token quotas when explaining eviction policy. When asked about cold-start KV warming, replied with generalities (prewarm + background sweep) but no concrete pipeline/metrics.
Behavioral/answers: when asked about a regression that increases 95th percentile latency by 30ms, immediately went to kernel-level investigation (schedulers/affinity) rather than staged rollout or feature flagging. Has deep infra instincts but less product-risk prioritization.
Pairing code: wrote clear helper functions, used comments, but did not thread cancellation contexts through async path. Left TODOs: "graceful-shutdown semantics" and "multi-tenant quotas".
Cultural signal: asks skeptical but good clarifying Qs. Mentions previous role at a mid-size infra company where they owned an edge cache service. Values observable metrics and fast feedback loops.
Red flags: small tendency to assume ops-level familiarity across teams; will push for low-level fixes that may break cross-team contracts unless coached.
behavioral_observations:
- Curious: asked follow-ups about our traffic shapes and tooling.
- Ownership: speaks in ownership language but examples are focused on personal code ownership rather than cross-org coordination.
- Communication: concise but sometimes jumps to technical details without high-level framing.
- Learning agility: good — asked about areas she didn't know and proposed experiments to learn (A/B on admission filter thresholds, synthetic traffic tests).
interview_questions_and_answers:
Q: How would you handle a model rollout that degrades quality for a subset of customers?
A: Immediate rollback and a postmortem; then instrument more granular metrics. Would prefer to test on a small canary. (no mention of automatic fallbacks or layered routing policies we use)

Q: Describe a memory leak you debugged.
A: Found stale references in a background worker — added weak refs and tightened lifecycle. Showed a reasonable root cause analysis and a plan to detect regressions via heap-dumps and sampling.

Q: How do you design for multi-tenant fairness?
A: Per-tenant quotas + priority buckets + circuit-breakers. Good conceptual answer but lacked concrete admission control algorithm tuned for dynamic LLM KV sizes.
strengths:
- Strong infra/debugging instincts.
- Practical caching ideas that could unlock cost wins.
- Good at measurable experiments and A/B thinking.
- Clean code style in pairing exercise.
weaknesses:
- Limited experience with product-level rollout policies and model-variant fallbacks (our key differentiator).
- Needs sharpening on multi-tenant economic tradeoffs (token billing interplay).
- Sometimes fixates on low-level fixes before exhausting higher-level mitigations.
open_questions:
- Would Velma be comfortable owning a customer-impacting oncall rotation or prefer to be a deep tech contributor without owner responsibilities?
- How quickly can she internalize our rollout/playbook conventions (canary -> automatic fallback -> region routing)?
- Is she motivated by product/merchant tradeoffs or primarily by systems craft?
action_items:
- Send two follow-up homework prompts: 1) sketch a canary+fallback policy for a model rollout (one page), 2) propose an admission-control algorithm for multi-tenant KV cache with cost considerations.
- If homework looks good, arrange a short sync with product/ops to probe cross-team instincts.
- Add Arjun as a secondary interviewer if we proceed to onsite.
decision_matrix_notes:
Fast hire if: homework shows product-level thinking and clear operational playbooks.
Pass if: homework is purely infra-craft without rollout/cost thinking.
Hire path: IC4 with explicit onboarding plan on rollouts + mentorship.
